thread.title: Texas sets record with over 35,000 applications on first day of school choice program
thread.title_full: Texas sets record with over 35,000 applications on first day of school choice program

author: L. V. Perez
title: Texas sets record with over 35,000 applications on first day of school choice program
text:
Texans submitted more than 35,000 applications for the Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program on its first day, marking a record-setting launch for a state-based school choice initiative. The application window opened Wednesday, and thousands of applications were received within the first hour. By noon, over 20,000 applications had been logged, according to Acting Texas Comptroller Kelly Hancock.
The TEFA program provides accounts that can be used to pay for tuition, tutoring, therapies, instructional materials, and other educational expenses. Most students will receive $10,474 through the program, while students with special needs may be eligible for up to $30,000. With a budget in the billions of dollars, TEFA is now the largest day-one school choice program launched by any state.
Families are encouraged to apply before the March 17 deadline. The application process takes about 15 minutes and is open to families with multiple children. The program does not operate on a first-come, first-served basis; all applicants have an equal chance regardless of when they apply during the window.
Nathan Cunneen, Texas State Director of the American Federation for Children, said: “The Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) program launched in true Texas style, with application figures eclipsing those of other states. This extraordinary response underscores Texans’ demand for school choice. If you have not yet applied for TEFA, please do so today by visiting educationfreedom.texas.gov.”
